issues.description: The problem statement and UML require Animal.messageOnFeed() to return a String (used directly in printing and song construction), but the solution's Animal.messageOnFeed() returns a FeedResponse object. This mismatch means the solution's types are incompatible with the specified API and with how Farm and the song expect to use messageOnFeed() as a String.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the API so messageOnFeed() has the same return type everywhere. Preferably follow the UML/problem statement: change Animal.messageOnFeed() in the solution to return String (public abstract String messageOnFeed()), update all subclasses (Seal, Pig, Goat) to return the expected String messages, remove or adapt the FeedResponse class, and ensure Farm and singFarmSong() print those Strings. Alternatively, if FeedResponse is intended, update the problem statement, UML, and template to specify and use FeedResponse consistently (including adjusting song printing to use FeedResponse.getMessage()).

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Animal.messageOnFeed() as returning a String (messageOnFeed(): String). The solution implementation defines Animal.messageOnFeed() returning a FeedResponse object (FeedResponse messageOnFeed()), and introduces a FeedResponse wrapper class. This mismatch in the conceptual representation of the feed message (String vs. FeedResponse) creates an API inconsistency that can confuse students: the exercise text and template expect a simple String message, while the solution uses a different type and abstraction for the same concept.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the API across artifacts. Either change the solution so Animal.messageOnFeed() returns String (and have subclasses return the feed message String) and remove or adapt FeedResponse, or update the problem statement and template to describe and require a FeedResponse return type and explain the wrapper class. Preferably return String across Animal and subclasses to match the UML and template expectations.
